1.

The present interlocutory application has been filed on behalf of the appellant for suspension of
sentence and grant of ad-interim bail during the pendency of this appeal.
2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the State.

3. The appellant has been convicted for the offence under Sections 304B/498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code and has been maximum sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for seven years with a fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default thereof, to undergo Simple Imprisonment for two months for the offence under Section 304(B)/34 of the IPC by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI- cum-Special Judge, C.A.W, Hazaribag in Sessions Trial No.138 of 2019.
4. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that due to burn injuries this appellant has treated his wife and it was accidental.
During treatment, she died.
Further, it has been submitted that the appellant has already completed more than half of the sentence as imposed by the learned Trial Court.
On the above basis, the prayer for bail has been made.
5. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for bail.

(i) The appellant will submit his mobile number before the learned court below which he will always keep active and will not change it during pendency of this case without prior permission of the court.
